INSTITUTIONAL PATHOLOGY REPORT
Accession: PATH-2024-88421 | Specimen: CT-guided core biopsy, right upper lobe lung mass

CLINICAL HISTORY: 54-year-old female, never smoker. CT chest shows 4.5 cm RUL spiculated mass with mediastinal adenopathy. ECOG 1.

DIAGNOSIS: Invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated (Grade 2), acinar predominant pattern.
Tumor size (biopsy fragment): estimated 45 mm on imaging correlation.
Lymphovascular invasion: Present.
Perineural invasion: Not identified.

IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY:
TTF-1: Positive
Napsin A: Positive
p40: Negative

MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY (FoundationOne CDx NGS):
EGFR exon 19 deletion (c.2235_2249del, p.E746_A750del) — VAF 42%
KRAS: No mutation detected
ALK (IHC): Negative
ROS1 (FISH): Negative
TP53: Wild-type
TMB: 4 Muts/Mb
PD-L1 IHC (22C3): Tumor Proportion Score 12%

---

RADIOLOGY REPORT — CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST
Indication: Staging of newly diagnosed lung malignancy.

Findings:
- 4.5 cm spiculated mass in the right upper lobe (RUL), no cavitation.
- Enlarged right paratracheal (station 4R) lymph node, 1.8 cm short axis.
- Enlarged subcarinal (station 7) lymph node, 1.5 cm short axis.
- No pleural effusion. No pleural invasion.
- No adrenal, hepatic, or osseous metastases identified.

Impression: Primary lung adenocarcinoma with mediastinal nodal involvement (N2). Clinical stage IIIA (T2aN2M0).

---

CLINICAL NOTES — MEDICAL ONCOLOGY CONSULT
Patient: 54F, never smoker.
PMH: Hypertension (amlodipine 5mg daily), mild intermittent asthma.
Allergies: Penicillin (rash).
Labs: Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL (eGFR ~78 mL/min), ALT 22 U/L, Hgb 12.4 g/dL, Plt 245K.
Weight: 62 kg.

Assessment: Newly diagnosed stage IIIA LUAD, EGFR exon 19 deletion, PD-L1 12%. ECOG 1.
Plan: Discuss first-line osimertinib vs chemoradiation per NCCN. Multidisciplinary tumor board referral.
Tumor board question: Candidate for definitive chemoradiation with durvalumab consolidation vs upfront osimertinib in unresectable stage III EGFR-mutated disease?
